content.content: {"result":"{\"success\": true, \"data\": {\"stdout\": \"\\\\begin{abstract}\\nVision-Language-Action (VLA) models report high Collision Avoidance Rates (CAR) on safety benchmarks, yet we show these metrics are contaminated by action collapse.\\nOn SafeLIBERO, an SDF-augmented Pi0 achieves 91.5\\\\% CAR while 99.6\\\\% of its safe episodes exhibit end-effector (EE) displacement below 0.1\\\\,mm; the robot is frozen, not safe.\\nWe present displacement-filtered CAR (dfCAR), which excludes sub-threshold episodes, as a corrective metric; the bimodal displacement distribution makes it robust across a $[2, 200]$\\\\,mm threshold range.\\nWe show that end-effector-only Signed Distance Field (SDF) supervision is neither necessary nor structurally sufficient for collision avoidance in our experimental setting.\\nIt is counterproductive at inference time: three ground-truth oracle variants all reduce CAR below unrefined baselines, as the SDF gradient repels the end-effector but drives arm links into obstacles.\\nIts contribution during training is dose-dependent: LoRA-only fine-tuning raises dfCAR from 26.8\\\\% to 54.83\\\\%$\\\\,\\\\pm\\\\,$2.25, matching SDF-augmented training at $\\\\lambda{=}0.005$ (54.5\\\\%$\\\\,\\\\pm\\\\,$2.29) and $\\\\lambda{=}0.01$ (56.33\\\\%$\\\\,\\\\pm\\\\,$1.61); at $\\\\lambda{=}0.1$, two of three seeds show a marginal signal (58.25\\\\%$\\\\,\\\\pm\\\\,$0.35, $p{\\\\approx}0.071$, two-tailed permutation test) whose per-task avoidance pattern still mirrors the demonstration distribution.\\nDisplacement filtering is necessary for meaningful VLA safety evaluation; EE-only geometric supervision cannot be credited with delivering collision avoidance, nor expected to do so.\\n\\\\end{abstract}\", \"stderr\": \"\", \"return_code\": 0}, \"error\": null, \"metadata\": {\"elapsed_seconds\": 0.52}}"}

{"success": true, "data": {"stdout": "\begin{abstract}
Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models report high Collision Avoidance Rates (CAR) on safety benchmarks, yet we show these metrics are contaminated by action collapse.
On SafeLIBERO, an SDF-augmented Pi0 achieves 91.5\% CAR while 99.6\% of its safe episodes exhibit end-effector (EE) displacement below 0.1\,mm; the robot is frozen, not safe.
We present displacement-filtered CAR (dfCAR), which excludes sub-threshold episodes, as a corrective metric; the bimodal displacement distribution makes it robust across a $[2, 200]$\,mm threshold range.
We show that end-effector-only Signed Distance Field (SDF) supervision is neither necessary nor structurally sufficient for collision avoidance in our experimental setting.
It is counterproductive at inference time: three ground-truth oracle variants all reduce CAR below unrefined baselines, as the SDF gradient repels the end-effector but drives arm links into obstacles.
Its contribution during training is dose-dependent: LoRA-only fine-tuning raises dfCAR from 26.8\% to 54.83\%$\,\pm\,$2.25, matching SDF-augmented training at $\lambda{=}0.005$ (54.5\%$\,\pm\,$2.29) and $\lambda{=}0.01$ (56.33\%$\,\pm\,$1.61); at $\lambda{=}0.1$, two of three seeds show a marginal signal (58.25\%$\,\pm\,$0.35, $p{\approx}0.071$, two-tailed permutation test) whose per-task avoidance pattern still mirrors the demonstration distribution.
Displacement filtering is necessary for meaningful VLA safety evaluation; EE-only geometric supervision cannot be credited with delivering collision avoidance, nor expected to do so.
\end{abstract}", "stderr": "", "return_code": 0}, "error": null, "metadata": {"elapsed_seconds": 0.52}}

Action collapse renders reported CAR illusory (\\\\S\\\\ref{sec:dfcar}); EE-only oracle refinement is counterproductive (\\\\S\\\\ref{sec:ee_only}); and collision-free demonstrations, not geometric supervision, account for all measured avoidance gains (\\\\S\\\\ref{sec:avoidance_source}).\\n\\n\\\\paragraph{Why EE-only SDF fails.}\\nTwo independent causes explain the null result. \\\\textit{(i)~Demonstration data subsumes the SDF signal.} Collision-free demonstrations implicitly encode spatial avoidance; the ${\\\\sim}$28\\\\,pp CAR gain arises entirely from this distributional shift, with per-task ordering invariant across all SDF conditions (\\\\S\\\\ref{sec:avoidance_source}). At low $\\\\lambda$, SDF is redundant; at $\\\\lambda = 0.1$, the marginal signal preserves the same demonstration-driven pattern. \\\\textit{(ii)~EE monitoring cannot prevent full-body collisions.} The SDF gradient acts on a single point while collisions occur along intermediate links. Oracle experiments confirm this: ground-truth SDF refinement \\\\emph{reduces} CAR by 6--10\\\\,pp below unrefined baselines (\\\\S\\\\ref{sec:ee_only}), because pushing the EE away rotates unmonitored links through obstacles. We hypothesize that collision-free demonstration trajectories implicitly encode workspace priors through their spatial distribution: the robot learns to favor regions of the workspace that are inherently collision-free, without requiring explicit geometric supervision. These two causes are independent; effective geometric safety requires both full-body supervision and training signals beyond demonstrations.\\n\\n\\\\paragraph{Implications for evaluation.}\\ndfCAR corrects action-collapse contamination using only EE position logging, already available in most evaluation pipelines. The bimodal displacement distribution makes $\\\\tau_d$ robust across five orders of magnitude. We recommend reporting both CAR and dfCAR; the gap quantifies contamination. This contamination spans a 4000$\\\\times$ parameter range (Pi0 Full-FT ${\\\\sim}$2.5B to Pi0+A1 ${\\\\sim}$658K trainable), a structural consequence of evaluating avoidance without verifying motion. More broadly, safety may need to operate at the planning or joint-space constraint layer, since any EE-centric loss inherits the same blind spot.\\n\\n\\\\paragraph{Limitations.}\\nOur evaluation covers one benchmark suite (SafeLIBERO, four tasks) and two model families (Pi0, Pi0.5). The tabletop setting with fixed-base manipulator and known obstacles may not generalize to mobile platforms and cluttered scenes. Oracle experiments used a largely frozen model (Pi0+A1, TSR${\\\\approx}$0\\\\%); testing on an actively moving policy would better isolate the structural limitation. """Auto-switch paper text based on λ=0.1 s2 30K eval result.

Usage:
  python paper_switch.py --s2-car 57.5 --s2-tsr 48.0 --dry-run
  python paper_switch.py --s2-car 57.5 --s2-tsr 48.0
"""
import argparse
import subprocess
import sys
from itertools import combinations
from math import comb, sqrt
from pathlib import Path

NULL_VALUES = [57, 52.5, 55, 57, 54, 52.5]
NULL_MEAN = sum(NULL_VALUES) / len(NULL_VALUES)
NULL_STD = (sum((x - NULL_MEAN) ** 2 for x in NULL_VALUES) / 5) ** 0.5

S0_CAR, S1_CAR = 58.0, 58.5
S0_TSR, S1_TSR = 47.0, 49.0

PAPER_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "docs" / "paper"


def mean(v):
    return sum(v) / len(v)


def std_b(v):
    m = mean(v)
    return (sum((x - m) ** 2 for x in v) / (len(v) - 1)) ** 0.5


def perm_test(null_vals, treat_vals):
    pool = null_vals + treat_vals
    k = len(treat_vals)
    obs = mean(treat_vals)
    mu = mean(pool)
    dev = abs(obs - mu)
    n = comb(len(pool), k)
    ge = tw = 0
    for c in combinations(pool, k):
        m = mean(c)
        if m >= obs:
            ge += 1
        if abs(m - mu) >= dev - 1e-12:
            tw += 1
    return ge / n, tw / n, n


def fill(tpl, vals):
    for k, v in vals.items():
        tpl = tpl.replace("{" + k + "}", str(v))
    return tpl


def safe_replace(content, old, new, label):
    n = content.count(old)
    if n == 0:
        print(f"  !! [{label}] NOT FOUND")
        return content, False
    if n > 1:
        print(f"  !! [{label}] found {n}x")
        return content, False
    return content.replace(old, new), True


def get_replacements(scenario, v):
    R = []
    is_c = scenario == "C"

    # 1. abstract.tex L7
    old = (
        r"Its contribution during training is dose-dependent: LoRA-only fine-tuning "
        r"raises dfCAR from 26.8\% to 54.83\%$\,\pm\,$2.25, matching SDF-augmented "
        r"training at $\lambda{=}0.005$ (54.5\%$\,\pm\,$2.29) and $\lambda{=}0.01$ "
        r"(56.33\%$\,\pm\,$1.61); at $\lambda{=}0.1$, two of three seeds show a "
        r"marginal signal (58.25\%$\,\pm\,$0.35, $p{\approx}0.071$, two-tailed "
        r"permutation test) whose per-task avoidance pattern still mirrors the "
        r"demonstration distribution."
    )
    if is_c:
        new = fill(
            r"Its contribution during training is dose-dependent: LoRA-only fine-tuning "
            r"raises dfCAR from 26.8\% to 54.83\%$\,\pm\,$2.25, matching SDF-augmented "
            r"training at $\lambda{=}0.005$ (54.5\%$\,\pm\,$2.29) and $\lambda{=}0.01$ "
            r"(56.33\%$\,\pm\,$1.61); at $\lambda{=}0.1$, a modest but statistically "
            r"significant increase emerges ({mean_car}\%$\,\pm\,${std_car}, permutation "
            r"$p{=}${p_value}, 3 seeds), though the effect size ({delta_pp}\,pp) is small "
            r"relative to the $+$28\,pp gain from fine-tuning alone, and per-task avoidance "
            r"patterns still mirror the demonstration distribution.", v)
    else:
        new = fill(
            r"SDF supervision during training adds no measurable benefit: LoRA-only "
            r"fine-tuning raises dfCAR from 26.8\% to 54.83\%$\,\pm\,$2.25, matching "
            r"SDF-augmented training across the full tested range $\lambda \in "
            r"\{0.005, 0.01, 0.1\}$ ($p{>}0.05$ for all; $\lambda{=}0.1$: "
            r"{mean_car}\%$\,\pm\,${std_car}, 3 seeds).", v)
    R.append(("abstract.tex", "abstract L7", old, new))

import numpy as np

base = "/root/autodl-tmp/eval_results"
experiments = [
    ("LoRA s0", f"{base}/lora_baseline_s0_reeval_safelibero_object_levelII_seed7.json"),
    ("LoRA s1", f"{base}/reeval_lora_s1_30k.json"),
    ("SDF λ=0.005 s0", f"{base}/reeval_sdf_s0_l005_30k.json"),
    ("SDF λ=0.005 s1", f"{base}/reeval_sdf_s1_l005_30k.json"),
    ("SDF λ=0.005 s2", f"{base}/reeval_sdf_s2_l005_30k.json"),
    ("SDF λ=0.01 s0", f"{base}/reeval_sdf_s0_l01_30k.json"),
    ("SDF λ=0.01 s1", f"{base}/reeval_sdf_s1_l01_30k.json"),
    ("SDF λ=0.01 s2", f"{base}/reeval_sdf_s2_l01_30k.json"),
]

thresholds_mm = [2, 5, 10, 20, 50, 100, 200, 300]

results = []
for label, path in experiments:
    with open(path) as f:
        data = json.load(f)

    episodes = []
    for task in data["results"]:
        episodes.extend(task["episodes"])

    print(f"{label}: {len(episodes)} episodes")

    for thresh_mm in thresholds_mm:
        thresh_m = thresh_mm / 1000.0
        active = [ep for ep in episodes if ep.get("max_ee_displacement", 0) >= thresh_m]
        if len(active) > 0:
            safe = sum(1 for ep in active if not ep.get("collided", True))
            dfCAR = safe / len(active) * 100
        else:
            dfCAR = None
        results.append({
            "label": label,
            "threshold_mm": thresh_mm,
            "dfCAR": round(dfCAR, 2) if dfCAR is not None else "",
            "n_active": len(active),
            "n_total": len(episodes)
        })

out = "/root/autodl-tmp/threshold_sensitivity_v2.csv"
with open(out, "w", newline="") as f:
    writer = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=["label", "threshold_mm", "dfCAR", "n_active", "n_total"])
    writer.writeheader()
    writer.writerows(results)

print(f"\nWritten to {out}")

    'Pi05 base': 'pi05_base_reeval_safelibero_object_levelII_seed7.json',
    'LoRA s0': 'lora_baseline_s0_reeval_safelibero_object_levelII_seed7.json',
    'LoRA s1': 'reeval_lora_s1_30k.json',
    'LoRA s2': 'eval_safelibero_object_all_levelII_30000_lora_baseline_seed7.json',
    'SDF005 s0': 'reeval_sdf_s0_l005_30k.json',
    'SDF005 s1': 'reeval_sdf_s1_l005_30k.json',
    'SDF005 s2': 'reeval_sdf_s2_l005_30k.json',

    'SDF01 s1': 'reeval_sdf_s1_l01_30k.json',
    'SDF01 s2': 'reeval_sdf_s2_l01_30k.json',
}

for label, fname in files.items():
    fp = os.path.join(base, fname)
    if not os.path.exists(fp):
        print(f'{label}: FILE NOT FOUND')
        continue
    with open(fp) as f:
        data = json.load(f)
    
    total_ep = 0
    total_success = 0
    total_safe = 0
    total_ssr = 0  # success AND safe
    
    for t in data['results']:
        for ep in t['episodes']:
            total_ep += 1
            if ep['success']:
                total_success += 1
            if not ep.get('collided', True):
                total_safe += 1
            if ep['success'] and not ep.get('collided', True):
                total_ssr += 1
    
    tsr = total_success / total_ep * 100
    car = total_safe / total_ep * 100
    ssr = total_ssr / total_ep * 100
    ssr_tsr = ssr / tsr if tsr > 0 else 0
    
    print(f"{label:15s} TSR={tsr:5.1f}  CAR={car:5.1f}  SSR={ssr:5.1f}  SSR/TSR={ssr_tsr:.3f}  (n={total_ep})")
